page.text:
Remove a person from the middle of a group photo, close the gap as if they were never there, and do it all without touching Photoshop. That option is now sitting inside Lightroom for anyone who has never gotten comfortable with layers and masks.
Glyn Dewis walks through the exact workflow using a shot from his I Am Lyme project, a picture he grabbed with the Scallop Diver Dorset crew at the end of a shoot. He starts by testing the built-in remove tool in Lightroom with generative AI checked, and the result is honest: the background rebuilds fairly well, but the arm and hand of the man beside him fall apart. Dewis is upfront that this video is for people who use Lightroom and stop there, not for anyone already living in Photoshop every day. His own wife is the example he reaches for, someone with phone pictures she'd love to tidy up but no interest in learning masks to do it.
The real method routes the image out to Adobe Firefly through the Photo menu, using the "Generating Firefly" option and then "Edit Photo." That sends the picture to the Firefly website, where Dewis picks his model from a list that includes Adobe's own Firefly Image 5 alongside partner models like ChatGPT's image model and Google Gemini 3.1. His prompt spells everything out: remove the person in the blue baseball cap, move the remaining three people close together, and keep the faces, hair, clothing, and coloring identical to the original. About a minute and a half later, the three men are standing together, the background is intact, and there's no sign anyone was cut out. He then shows how to check the resolution and upscale, since the regenerated image comes back smaller than the 6,060 by 4,040 original.
Credit cost is where the tradeoffs get concrete. Switching to the ChatGPT image model at high quality jumps the cost from 20 credits to 80, a real leap that Dewis flags plainly. His framing is sensible: this is an occasional job, not a daily habit, so a single 80-credit edit won't drain your balance. He also points out the one rough edge in the round trip, that Firefly hands the finished file to your downloads folder rather than dropping it straight back into the Lightroom catalog, and he'd like Adobe to close that loop.
This fits into a wider shift in how Adobe is spreading generative editing across its apps instead of locking it behind Photoshop. Firefly now sits at the center of that push, and the model picker inside it, offering ChatGPT and Gemini alongside Adobe's own engine, points to a future where you choose the right tool for a specific edit rather than committing to one. The practical takeaway extends past removing people: a prompt that names exactly what to keep, faces, hair, clothing, coloring, gives generative models far less room to invent things you don't want. That discipline carries over to any AI edit you attempt, whether you're clearing a background, removing a distraction, or reworking a crowded holiday frame. Match the resolution question to your output too, since a regenerated file often lands smaller than your camera's native file and benefits from an upscale before you print or crop.
Dewis is careful not to oversell it. He says outright that Firefly isn't better than Photoshop, and if you're comfortable there, keep going. The point is that skipping Photoshop no longer puts this kind of edit out of reach, and the work doesn't have to be professional to be worth doing. A family photo with someone you'd rather not see, a holiday shot with a stranger drifting through the back, or a snap you simply want to like a bit more all qualify.

full: Вбудований інструмент Remove з увімкненим генеративним AI добре відновив фон, але зіпсував руку сусіда. Робочий метод — меню Photo → Generating Firefly → Edit Photo: кадр іде на сайт Firefly, де можна обрати модель — Firefly Image 5, модель зображень ChatGPT або Google Gemini 3.1. Промпт описує, кого прибрати, як зсунути решту людей і що зберегти незмінним (обличчя, волосся, одяг, кольори). Через приблизно півтори хвилини троє людей стоять поруч без слідів монтажу.

Ціна в кредитах: перемикання на модель ChatGPT у високій якості піднімає вартість з 20 до 80 кредитів за правку. Регенерований файл повертається меншим за оригінал 6060×4040, тож потрібен апскейл, а готовий результат падає в папку завантажень, а не в каталог Lightroom.
Автор підкреслює: Firefly не кращий за Photoshop, але такі правки більше не потребують шарів і масок, що відкриває їх звичайним користувачам з телефонними знімками.
means: Adobe робить видалення й перекомпонування людей доступним прямо з Lightroom через сторонні моделі (ChatGPT, Gemini) — це територія нашого Erase та GenErase. Показові вузькі місця: втрата роздільної здатності, розрив каталогу і 80 кредитів за правку. Luminar Neo може виграти, якщо GenErase поверне результат у повній роздільній здатності в межах каталогу й з прозорими лімітами, а Luminar Mobile — дати промпт-керування Erase для сімейних фото.

New models sell AI, but buyers still pick battery, speed
The smartphone’s upgrade pitch may now be AI, but consumers are still starting with the processor, with 29% of buyers ranking the chip as their top consideration when choosing their next smartphone in the first quarter of 2026, up from 24% a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research.
The finding comes as smartphone makers are packing AI into devices across price segments, from flagship phones that can translate conversations and search files using natural language to more affordable models offering AI photo editing, transcription and generative tools.
An Amazon India survey of more than 40,000 respondents conducted in July found that AI features influence the purchase decision of 82% of smartphone buyers. Contextual assistance was the most wanted AI capability, cited by 25% of respondents, followed by generative photo editing at 18% and visual search at 17%.
Yet Amazon’s data also reinforces Counterpoint’s finding that the fundamentals remain important. Performance and speed were the biggest purchase drivers at 87%, followed by battery life at 79% and camera quality at 77%. Battery, in particular, remains a weakness. It was the aspect consumers most frequently said their current smartphone needs to improve, at 22%, ahead of camera at 17% and performance at 12%.
“While AI has moved from a talking point to an expectation, customers are just as clear about the fundamentals that still matter, like performance, battery and camera. They are also willing to pay more for the device that gets it right,” said Zeba Khan, director, consumer electronics, Amazon India.
“Consumers still value the fundamentals of a fast, responsive and reliable device. With increasing tech literacy and rapid innovation, consumers are now looking for the right combination of features that best fits their usage needs,” said Arushi Chawla, consumer research lead and senior analyst at Counterpoint.
The latest launches all add AI to the traditional smartphone formula of processor, camera, battery and display. Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max launched last year elevated Apple Intelligence, launched in 2024, with Image Background, Notify Me and Call Context features, adding to live translation, writing and summarisation tools and visual intelligence. This year’s models, to be announced on September 9, are rumoured to have A20 Pro chip to optimise on-device Apple Intelligence, along with possibly the brand’s first foldable smartphone.
Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z Fold8 and higher-tier Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra integrates Galaxy AI across devices. Google’s Pixel 11 Pro, launched on August 12, offers deeper Gemini integration.
The AI push is also moving into phones outside the flagship segment. OnePlus’ N6 offers AI editing tools such as AI Eraser and AI Reflection Eraser. OPPO’s Reno16 5G brings AI into the hardware and a personal memory system integrating assistants including Gemini, Perplexity and ChatGPT. Vivo’s S2 5G has AI Creation and Transcript Assist. Xiaomi’s Redmi Note 15 series brings Google Gemini, Circle to Search and Xiaomi HyperAI.
Nothing’s Phone (4b) uses Essential Space to parse screenshots and voice notes and turn them into tasks and reminders, alongside AI Eraser, voice transcription and ChatGPT-integrated widgets.
Rather than being viewed as another standalone specification, AI is increasingly embedded across tools. “As a result, AI is evolving into a feature-level consideration that can influence consumer preference and, in some cases, trigger a purchase decision,” Chawla added.
“I think smartphone differentiation is moving away from individual specifications and towards the overall user experience. Value for money will always matter, but it is becoming harder for brands built primarily around that proposition to stand out, particularly in a market where consumers are being asked to spend more,” said Akis Evagelidis, co-founder and India president of Nothing. “When you are making a bigger purchase, you want to feel that you are getting something meaningfully better, not just a longer specification sheet. This is where we believe Nothing has a strong advantage,” he added. “Our recent Phone (4b) delivered our biggest smartphone opening to date and became Flipkart’s best-selling smartphone above Rs 30,000 on Day One,” Evagelidis said.
Apple sees AI as integral to the existing smartphone experience. Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice-president of software engineering, said in a blog post: “Truly helpful AI must be centered on our users’ needs, deeply integrated into the products they rely on every day, grounded in personal context, and built with privacy at every step.”
OPPO sees the shift particularly in how users interact with the phone. “While camera and design will always remain important, consumers are increasingly looking at how intelligently a smartphone can adapt to the way they work, create, travel and go about their day,” said an OPPO India spokesperson.
Samsung is taking the argument beyond the individual handset and towards the wider ecosystem. “AI is getting smarter faster, and this will continue. But to change how people live, it must answer: where, how and into whose hands does this intelligence reach? This will define AI’s next chapter,” Samsung Electronics CEO and President TM Roh wrote in a blog post.
That ecosystem is becoming increasingly relevant as smartphones face competition from devices that can perform functions once associated mainly with the phone. Smartwatches handle health tracking, earbuds handle calls and voice interactions, laptops increasingly have AI assistants and smart glasses are being developed for navigation, translation and contextual information. Even OpenAI is reportedly preparing an AI-first consumer device, developed with former Apple design chief Jony Ive’s LoveFrom studio and expected in 2027. The first device is expected to be compact and screenless, while OpenAI’s longer-term ambition is reportedly to develop hardware that could eventually replace the smartphone.
For now, the smartphone remains the central device because of its portability, connectivity, app ecosystem and ability to integrate with other devices, according to Counterpoint’s Chawla.

Photoshop's autofocus point checker inside Camera Raw 18.6 shows you exactly which points your camera locked onto, so you can catch a blurred watch face or a hand in focus before you commit to the wrong shot. That single feature answers a question you've probably asked yourself a hundred times while culling: did the camera focus where I thought it did?
Unmesh Dinda runs through 20 recent additions to Photoshop and Camera Raw, and the autofocus overlay is just the opener. Right-click a raw file, select show autofocus points, and the exact focus points appear on the image. Zoom in and the story gets clear fast. Dinda demonstrates it on a watch, where one frame nails the face and another lands on his hand instead. The shortcut is Command Option Shift O on Mac, Control Alt Shift O on Windows, and it turns the overlay on and off instantly.
Several of the strongest updates sit in Camera Raw itself. The new glow effect lives in the effects dropdown and gives you three distinct styles: diffusion, which softens highlights; bloom, which adds light on top of highlights; and halation, which wraps a colored edge around bright areas. Dinda runs it as a smart filter so it stays editable, and he shows how the highlight slider controls whether only the brightest points glow or whether softer highlights get pulled in too. There's also a vectorscope now, borrowed from video color grading, which maps where your colors land and doubles as a skin tone checker when you turn on the skin tone indicator. Match your skin tones to that diagonal line using point color, and uneven complexions fall into place.
The Camera Raw generative expand deserves attention because it works on raw files while keeping every setting intact. Enable expand in the crop section, drag out the canvas, click generate, and the extended area carries your white balance, highlights, and shadows with no visible seam. Dinda points out that this is impossible in Photoshop proper, where expansion happens on a baked-in version of the image. The blemish removal tool in the remove section keeps real skin texture instead of smoothing everything into plastic, with separate sliders for spots and for moles or birthmarks. If you'd rather avoid AI entirely, you can switch off every generative feature under the settings cog.
The through-line worth grabbing here is that Adobe keeps moving raw-native editing forward while adding a parallel AI workspace that hides layers and channels completely. Photoshop 27.1 introduced the AI-assisted mode, with markup tools, region selection, and a tune beta that shifts a scene from day to evening. That split reflects a wider shift across the industry, where destructive one-click results and precise nondestructive control now live under one roof. The practical takeaway is to treat the two as different jobs. Reach for the AI workspace when you want a fast rendered concept, then hit pro editor to drop the full image back into Photoshop for real masking, dodging, and compositing. Understanding masks, focus, and light is what lets you decide which tool actually earns the edit, rather than accepting whatever the model hands back.
A few quieter changes save time in daily work. You can now customize the save dialog file format under Edit, dragging formats like IFF and PCX out of the list so save a copy stops burying the options you use. The metadata info panel reads camera model, settings, and content credentials, and clicking the location opens the exact spot in Google Maps. Dynamic fit resizes text to fill any shape you draw, including a path made with the pen tool, adjusting the font size as you type. Color wheels have moved into masking too, so you can grade a background in one direction and your subject in another. Two new mask sliders, feather and edge, let you contract or expand a selection and soften it, which pairs well with shallow depth-of-field shots where a hard mask edge gives you away.
Give the video above a full watch to see the remaining features Dinda demonstrates, including render to DNG and the halation glow trick stacked on top of a bloom.

full: Camera Raw 18.6 показує точки автофокусу з RAW-файлу (правий клік → Show autofocus points, Cmd+Opt+Shift+O), що допомагає відсіювати кадри з промахом фокуса. У блоці Effects з'явився Glow з трьома стилями — Diffusion, Bloom, Halation; додано вектороскоп з індикатором тону шкіри, а колірні кола й повзунки Feather/Edge перенесені в маски.

Generative Expand у Camera Raw працює безпосередньо з RAW і зберігає баланс білого, світла й тіні без видимого шва — у самому Photoshop розширення можливе лише на запеченому зображенні. Інструмент видалення плям (blemish removal) залишає реальну текстуру шкіри з окремими повзунками для плям і родимок. Усі генеративні функції можна вимкнути в налаштуваннях.

Photoshop 27.1 отримав AI-режим без шарів і каналів: розмітка, вибір областей і бета-функція Tune, що переводить сцену з дня у вечір. Автор радить використовувати AI-режим для швидких концептів, а «Pro editor» — для масок і композитингу.
means: Adobe закриває одразу кілька наших ніш: Glow конкурує з Magic Light AI та Atmosphere AI, blemish removal із збереженням текстури — зі Skin AI, GenExpand на RAW із збереженням проявки — з нашим GenExpand, а Tune «день → вечір» перетинається з Relight AI та Twilight Enhancer. Оверлей точок автофокусу — дешева функція для кулінгу, якої в Neo немає. Окремий AI-режим без шарів підтверджує нашу ставку на простий інтерфейс.

This week, Camera Intelligence revealed the latest generative AI features in its Caira camera: adding Nano Banana video editing to its genAI photography. It was the latest reminder that the imaging industry, like the rest of the world, is doubling down on AI in its products – including the generative kind.
No hate, no shade. But it reminded me of a conversation I had with Canon earlier this year, when I asked the Japanese leadership about the subject of AI – and they were crystal clear about what is and what is not off limits when it comes to artificial intelligence.
"AI is going to keep on playing an important role for any shooting experiences for our products," said Tetsushi Hibi, advisory director of Canon's Img Optical Business Unit 1, behind closed doors at the CP+ 2026 show in Japan.
"So this is Canon’s stance: we are going to use AI not to generate imagery, but to capture scenes as close to the reality of shooting as possible – noise reduction, color correction, distortion correction, aberration – so those are the functions we are aiming to put it onto in our products."
We've already seen this in practice, particularly with the Canon EOS R1 and R5 Mark II – both of which use Canon's neural network image processing (NnIP) for features like 400% in-camera upscaling and 2-stop noise reduction. And of course, the many algorithmic subject detection and tracking options.
It is heartening to know, however, that generative AI imaging is not on the table for Canon – particularly with the company having rolled out its Authenticity Imaging System in May, offering content compliance to help verify the authenticity of images (and, by proxy, policing image manipulation and AI embelishment).
Where Canon definitely is implementing AI, however, is in the design phase.

"We have started our attempt to use AI for design," notes Hibi, which is born out by a recent company report that AI will be used in the early prototyping phase to simulate things like drop tests and assess thermal performance.
"We have no choice but to use AI in the design department," adds Go Tokura, executive vice president and head of Canon's Imaging Group. He's also sure to point out that the fruits of the technology will still be distinctly 'Canon', rather than resulting in homogenized products that are the same as other brands.
"When it comes to design, it is said that the AI can bring up the best possible solution. And you may think, if that’s the case, every single company will come up with the same new products.
"We have our own accumulated technology – not just designing capabilities, but also production technology as well, and materials. So even if we use AI for design, AI will consider all these unique capabilities to come up with the best solution for Canon .
"So even if the solution is generated by AI, that could be a good solution that will be able to differentiate our product from the others."

title: Canon: AI у камерах — для шумозаглушення й корекції, а не генерації зображень
lead: Керівництво Canon на CP+ 2026 заявило Digital Camera World, що використовуватиме AI лише для наближення знімка до реальності — денойз, корекція кольору, дисторсії та аберацій — і не планує генеративних функцій у камерах.
full: Тецуші Хібі з Canon Image Optical Business Unit 1 окреслив позицію компанії: AI має покращувати захоплення сцени, а не створювати зображення. Це вже реалізовано у EOS R1 та R5 Mark II через нейромережеву обробку NnIP: апскейл 400% у камері, шумозаглушення на 2 стопи, AI-розпізнавання й трекінг об'єктів. У травні Canon також запустила систему Authenticity Imaging для верифікації справжності знімків.

Привід для статті — камера Caira від Camera Intelligence, яка додала генеративне відеоредагування на Nano Banana до своїх genAI-фотофункцій. Canon натомість застосовує AI у проєктуванні: симуляції дроп-тестів і теплового режиму на етапі прототипування.
means: Виробники камер переносять денойз і апскейл у сам корпус (2 стопи шуму, 400% апскейл на R1/R5 II), що поступово зменшує потребу в Noiseless AI та Upscale AI на десктопі для нових камер Canon. Водночас генеративне редагування Canon свідомо залишає софту — це простір для GenErase, GenSwap, Sky AI. Тренд на верифікацію справжності (Authenticity Imaging, Content Credentials) варто врахувати в експорті з Luminar Neo.

page.text:
Photoshop's Brightness/Contrast slider is gone, replaced by a new Light adjustment layer that pulls Camera Raw controls straight into the main editor. Exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, and blacks now live in a single panel that behaves like a nondestructive version of the Camera Raw sliders many of you already trust.
Aaron Nace of PHLEARN walks through the layer and lands on a strong recommendation: skip the old Brightness/Contrast algorithm entirely. He explains that the Light layer is the newest arrival in a growing line that already includes Grain, Clarity, Dehaze, and Color. If you preferred the old behavior, double-click the Light layer, open the small hidden menu on the right side of the Properties panel, and switch the version to "Legacy." That brings Brightness/Contrast back exactly as it was, so nobody loses the tool they built their workflow around.
Slider order carries real weight here, and Nace lays out the sequence he uses every time: exposure first, then whites and blacks, then highlights and shadows, and contrast dead last. He also stresses masking. By default, a Light layer affects the entire frame, so he starts with Select Subject on the background layer before creating the adjustment, which turns the selection into a mask automatically. From there he inverts the mask with Command or Control plus I to work the background separately, dropping exposure to push the subject forward and lifting the whites to pull detail back into the sky. He repeats the process on a second Light layer for the subject alone, keeping each adjustment isolated and fully reversible.
The glow effect is where the tutorial earns a closer look. Nace stacks a third Light layer, groups it with itself using Command or Control plus G, then adds a mask to the group and paints in a radial gradient behind the figure. That double-mask trick, one on the layer and one on the group, is the part worth watching him do slowly, because the logic behind why it works is easy to lose if you only read the steps.
This shift fits a pattern Adobe has been running for a while now. Camera Raw and Lightroom have long been the home for exposure and tone work, and Photoshop is steadily absorbing those same controls as editable layers. If you shoot in raw and process there before opening a file, the Light layer lets you keep that same mental model instead of switching tools halfway through an edit. The bigger takeaway is the masking discipline itself: isolating exposure and tone to specific regions, subject versus background, is the same principle behind classic dodge and burn, and it transfers to any adjustment layer in the panel. Learn it on Light and it pays off on Color, Curves, and everything else. One quirk to expect: when you edit a layer beneath a Light layer, Photoshop temporarily hides the Light layers above it so you can see the raw effect you're adjusting. Nace demonstrates this with Grain, and it looks like a bug until you understand Adobe built it on purpose.
He also spends time on the Color layer, which brings temperature, tint, and vibrance sliders into the same nondestructive workflow, warming the image and nudging the tint toward green to match the tones already in the scene.

Google is integrating more of its services with AI, as the company announced that its personal agent, Gemini Spark, can now manage your Google Photos library. That means you can ask Gemini Spark to execute tasks in Google Photos, like editing images, curating albums, automatically creating shared albums with your favorite shots, turning concert flyer photos into calendar appointments, running workflows, and more.
On Thursday evening, Google Photos lead Shimrit Ben-Yair shared the new capabilities in a post on X , noting that the new capabilities would roll out over the next few weeks to eligible Gemini AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the U.S. in English.
The company didn’t say if or when it would roll out more broadly to international markets.
For a while now, I’ve relied on @GeminiApp and @antigravity agents across a wide range of use cases—spanning creativity, productivity, and analysis. But I’ve always dreamed of having a power agent to help me get the most out of my 143,206 photos and videos. And that day has come!… pic.twitter.com/WbnkYpattQ
The addition is yet another example of Google attempting to find product-market fit in terms of making AI appealing to consumers — in this case, by automating tedious tasks and helping people manage what are now often sizable photo libraries.
The move comes at a time when the AI industry is reckoning with the fact that it hasn’t properly sold the promise of AI to consumers. This week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bloomberg that the industry has “done a terrible job” communicating the benefits of technology, which has led to backlash from communities around the world.
Announcements like this from Google are part of the problem. While they may make certain tasks easier, on their own, such features don’t seem revolutionary or even, really, necessary. (It’s not that difficult to make a photo album after all.) But the competitive nature of the AI industry is pushing companies to promote every AI-infused upgrade, no matter how small, instead of waiting until the company can tell a broader story about how AI has shaped its software for the better.
To use Gemini Spark with Google Photos, you’ll need to first connect Google Photos to Gemini, then toggle on Spark in the top corner of the Gemini app, and enter your prompt.

You’re back from a fabulous holiday, now all that’s left is the daunting task of sorting through your thousands and thousands of travel photographs. To organise and sort his travel pictures, Will Cheung took the easy route and turned to Excire Foto 2027 There’s nothing like travel to get your creative juices flowing and the shutter finger working. For my recent holiday to Hong Kong, I didn’t have huge photographic ambitions, so I packed what I would consider a decent outfit because I didn’t want to get caught short, but neither did I take the kitchen sink approach.
At the heart of my kit was a couple of cameras, the Canon EOS R5 and EOS R5 Mark II , and they were supported by four zooms: a RF 14-35mm f/4 IS USM, RF 24-105mm f/4 IS USM, RF 70-200mm f/2.8L IS USM and RF 100-500mm f/4.5-7.1L IS USM.
The final lens was one I used a lot and that was a RF 28mm f/2.8 STM prime which was small, portable and reasonably fast. A Gitzo Series 1 Traveler carbon tripod and a set of Kase Armour filters rounded off my outfit. So quite a gear collection, but on days out in Hong Kong I only took out what I would use rather than what I thought I might use.
For urban walks I took the three zooms covering from 14mm to 200mm, while on the few occasions we went to parks or nature reserves, the RF 100-500mm f/4.5-7.1L IS USM was the mainstay and that was great for butterflies, dragonflies and birds.
Working through 24,000 raw images, the easy way
Over the fortnight’s holiday I took close to 24,000 raws, which is quite productive considering that photography was not the top priority and I just wanted a great break in a lovely city. On trips where I know I’m going to be busy with the camera I take my MacBook Air laptop and a portable external hard drive and at end of each day I would upload the shots into a folder with the date and location where I had been. There are two reasons for this. One, as back up in case something happens to the memory card. Two, this speeds up my workflow when I get home and with all my photos in folders ready to transfer to my storage hard drives. It sounds a tad fussy but it’s a system that works for me and putting in a little effort each night saves time back at base.
Another big time saver in my workflow is Excire Foto 2027, an AI-powered image management software that I use it to keep my 800,000 plus images organised.
I used to rely on Adobe Lightroom for this but now I cull rejects and images I’ll never use in Excire Foto 2027 first. Sifting through thousands of raw shots in Lightroom, rating and deleting as you go, is slow compared with Excire Foto 2027 where flicking through a serious number of images is a treat rather than a chore.
Large previews are refreshed almost instantly and there’s no waiting for images to sharpen up and once the shoot is thinned down, it’s imported into Lightroom for editing.
Using Excire Foto 2027 with existing images is straightforward too and once images are rated, the details can be transferred to current Lightroom catalogues. I started working with its predecessor, Excire Foto 2025, a couple of years ago but when Excire Foto 2027 was unveiled earlier this year all the improvements made upgrading to the latest version the obvious thing to do.
All the search features are available but now there is AI Text Recognition, Map view which takes GPS details from files and shows where photos were taken and a Timeline function where you view images taken at a particular time, even down to a specific day. There’s also an improved interface with a new-look search bar and Survey view where you can select a number of images which are displayed against a plain black background and as images are eliminated the remaining get bigger. It makes the funnelling down the selections a pleasure.
Automatic keywording is an incredibly useful skill of Excire Foto 2027 and another potential time saver and if, like me, you lack commitment in the keywording department, having a software do it for you is a good thing. Find by Text Prompt is a powerful, effective and versatile search tool. Just type in what you are looking for, which might be a specific subject, but you can try describing a particular theme or emotion and Excire Foto 2027 will use its AI powers to find suitable images. To show its effectiveness, I knew I had taken quite a few images of Hong Kong trams on my trip, so I performed a Find by Text Prompt search for ‘Hong Kong trams’ through the entire 800,000 image database. In a few seconds Excire Foto 2027 accurately identified 3650 tram images.
If you’ve spent a lot of money and time on kit and travel, it stands to reason that looking after your images is important and any process or software that can help should be considered. Excire Foto 2027 is fast and easy to use, boasts very powerful search tools and has an impressive line-up of photographer-friendly features. If you find managing your images time-consuming and even painful, Excire Foto 2027 could be your ideal solution.
The new Excire Foto 2027 app retains all the rating, culling and search skills of Foto 2025 plus it has gained several significant features.
AI Text Recognition gives a new way of searching the image database and the software will automatically detect visible text in your images, and it does this quickly. It means if you’re looking for a place name, street, shop front or brand name, you can do it accurately and very quickly.
Another major feature is Map View. Excire Foto 2027 automatically detects GPS data – whether embedded at the time or added post-shoot – in your images and videos and places where you shot the content on an interactive map.
Click on an appropriate location and you immediately see all the images shot there. It’s a great tool for travel, street and landscape photographers.
If you need to find images taken at a particular time frame, there’s a powerful timeline tool and it’s intuitive to use too. Just zoom into the timeline graph and the date you are looking for, and you see the images instantly and then you can rate, keyword and discard your work as normal.

full: Автор використовує Excire Foto 2027 для бібліотеки з понад 800 000 зображень: великі превʼю оновлюються майже миттєво, відбір браку проходить значно швидше, ніж у Lightroom, а рейтинги потім переносяться в наявні каталоги Lightroom. AI content creation platform, Picsart, has appointed Lusine Yeghiazaryan as Chief Financial Officer as the company shifts its focus from photo editing toward a video-first, AI-powered production model.
Yeghiazaryan joins from SADA Systems, where she served as CFO and oversaw the company’s expansion into new services and AI revenue segments, managed a partnership with Google Cloud and led SADA’s strategic sale to Insight Enterprises. Her career also includes management roles at Diebold Nixdorf, Deloitte and GoPro.
Picsart, which has more than 100 million monthly active users and over 2.5 billion downloads, is expanding beyond its origins as a photo-editing platform into what the company describes as a comprehensive creative technology stack.
The company reports that its users have created more than 1.1 billion AI videos and images since launch, with year-to-date AI usage up 270 per cent year-on-year based on internal data from August 2025 to August 2026.
The platform’s ecosystem now includes video-first tools, a Creative AI Agent Marketplace, CLI and MCP integration compatible with Claude and Codex, and desktop expansion via AI Playground.
As CFO, Yeghiazaryan will lead global financial strategy, with an initial focus on aligning Picsart’s financial trajectory with its video-first direction while balancing fiscal discipline with the pace of investment required for AI-led growth.
Founder and CEO of Picsart, Hovhannes Avoyan, framed the appointment as arriving at a turning point for both the company and the creative technology market.
“As AI and video transform how people create and communicate, we are focused on scaling the opportunities with the greatest potential to drive long-term growth and value,” Avoyan explained. “Lusine’s experience building and guiding high-growth technology businesses will be instrumental as we execute on that ambition.”
Yeghiazaryan pointed to the combination of Picsart’s user base, consumer engagement and market positioning as factors in her decision to join.
“Picsart has the rare combination of global scale, strong consumer affinity and significant upside across some of technology’s most dynamic markets,” Yeghiazaryan commented. “I’m excited to help shape the company’s next chapter by pairing ambitious investment in AI and video with disciplined execution and a clear focus on monetisation and value creation.”

Google has released Snapseed 4.0 for Android after nearly two years without a major update. The users will now enjoy Smart Masking, Batch Editing, and an in-app camera with real-time film emulation.
The update transforms Google’s photo editing application from a simple editing tool into an all-in-one shoot-and-edit platform while remaining completely free without subscriptions, watermarks, or in-app purchases.
Snapseed 4.0 introduces Smart Masking technology that allows users to isolate subjects or backgrounds with a single tap, eliminating manual brush work for targeted edits. The Batch Editing feature enables photographers to apply favorite looks and specific adjustments across multiple photos simultaneously. Android users previously relied on version 2.22 from 2024 while iOS users accessed advanced features through version 3.0 released in June 2025. Snapseed product lead Giles Ochs announced the Android release through Instagram, stating the wait was almost over after months of user requests.
The Snapseed Camera component provides real-time film emulation inspired by classic film stocks including Kodak Portra, Fujifilm Superia, Polaroid SX-70, and Ilford HP5. Users capture photos directly within Snapseed using custom styles or film looks with real-time effects that remain editable or reversible after shooting. Pro mode offers manual controls for ISO, Shutter Speed, and Focus settings. The viewfinder supports six color themes including Editor, Dusk, Negative, Steel, Haze, and Depth for different shooting aesthetics.
Google redesigned the interface with a new homepage grid displaying previously edited photos. Users tap Add Photo at the bottom to access the system file picker while a floating action button provides quick access to Snapseed Camera. The revamped toolbox helps users discover new editing types faster with streamlined navigation allowing parameter and mode changes with fewer taps. Users can now pin unlimited favorite tools instead of the previous four-tool limit while viewing images and tool options simultaneously through combined carousels and sliders.
New editing tools include Color HSL for hue, saturation, and luminance adjustments, Dehaze for atmospheric clarity, Halation adding red halos around bright lights mimicking film characteristics, and Bloom making bright lights bloom into neighboring areas. The update maintains over 30 professional tools spanning Healing, Selective adjustments, Lens Blur, Curves, Double Exposure, and various filters. Google implemented non-destructive editing allowing users to modify or reset adjustments without permanently altering original images.
Google began the staged rollout May 8 with the Play Store listing updated to version 4.0. Users who do not see the update immediately should receive it within coming days as Google expands availability. The iOS version received simultaneous updates to version 4.0 adding the new interface plus Halation and Bloom tools. Google vice president of Photos Shimrit Ben-Yair confirmed the rollout brings a more modern and fun user interface making editing faster, easier, and more powerful.
Industry observers noted Snapseed’s commitment to remaining free stands out in 2026 as nearly every capable mobile editing app has adopted monthly subscription models. Google acquired Snapseed developer Nik Software in 2012 and released major redesigns in 2017 before the application entered maintenance mode with minimal updates through 2024. The massive version jump from 2.22 to 4.0 signals Google’s renewed commitment to the 15-year-old photo editing platform that maintains popularity despite competition from Google Photos Magic Editor and subscription-based alternatives.

Presets that carry AI masks are the trick most landscape shooters overlook, and they can shave real minutes off every edit. Fall gives you a short window of color, cool air, and quieter parks, so the less time you spend clicking through the same steps in Lightroom Classic, the more frames you bring home.
Building a workflow around virtual copies and reusable masks is exactly what Terry Vander Heiden walks through, using three shots from Grand Teton National Park. Vander Heiden starts with a shortcut worth memorizing: highlight a batch of images, hold Shift to select the range, then press Command and the apostrophe key to spin up virtual copies of everything at once. That gives you a safe copy to experiment on while your original stays untouched. From there, he moves into a black-and-white conversion that leans on the clipping view rather than guesswork. Tapping the letter J lights up the highlight and shadow warnings, and holding the Option or Alt key while dragging the white and black sliders shows you precisely where detail burns out or crushes to pure black.
Once the tones are set, the color mixer becomes the real workspace for black and white. Vander Heiden pushes the reds to make the snow on the peaks separate, warms the oranges and yellows to lift the foliage, and drops the blues to darken the sky into something with punch. He then saves the whole recipe as a custom preset called "black and white landscape," which he's clear about treating as a starting point instead of a finished look. His stance on presets is refreshingly practical: you don't need to buy someone else's, you build your own to match how you like your images, then hover over other shots to preview the same settings before committing. That habit alone changes how fast you can move through a card full of similar frames.
The part that pays off most is masking. Lightroom's AI-driven landscape masks split an image into sky, mountains, vegetation, water, and natural ground automatically, and Vander Heiden bakes those masks straight into a preset so they regenerate on any new photo. Apply the preset, wait a second or two, and every mask appears fresh for that specific image rather than copied blindly from another. If Lightroom can't find something, say natural ground, it flags the mask with a small yield sign and you simply delete it. He shows both approaches: one preset that carries your actual adjustments for a run of near-identical shots, and a leaner preset that only generates the masks so you're free to edit each one on its own terms.
The bigger shift here is treating your catalog like an assembly line before you ever touch a slider. Bring a full trip's worth of landscapes in, run the mask preset across all of them, and every image is now pre-segmented and ready. This mirrors how Lightroom's masking has evolved since Adobe introduced AI-based Select Sky and Select Subject, then expanded into object detection that now recognizes distinct scene elements. Leaning on that means your local adjustments stop being one-off manual selections and become repeatable moves you can dial the same way every time. For anyone shooting the same location across a week, that consistency is what keeps a set of photos looking like they belong together, and it frees you to make creative calls on light and color instead of redrawing the same gradient over a ridgeline again and again. It fits best when your images share a structure, a horizon, a mountain line, a foreground of grass or water, which is precisely what fall landscape trips tend to produce.
Vander Heiden also covers housekeeping that keeps the panel clean, including hiding the portrait presets you'll never use through the manage presets menu and deleting user presets you no longer need, with a fair warning that deletions can't be recovered.

full: Маски Lightroom, засновані на розпізнаванні сцени, можна запекти у користувацький пресет. Автор показує два варіанти: пресет із повним набором правок для серії схожих кадрів і «легкий» пресет, який лише створює маски, залишаючи редагування вручну. Варто перевірити, чи наші Presets із локальними правками на Mask AI відпрацьовують так само автоматично на новому знімку, і показати це в комунікації.

Photoroom has launched Visual Agents for enterprise product catalogues, a system designed to manage AI image and video production for retailers and marketplaces.
The product builds workflows around incoming catalogue images, selects editing models for each task, checks the output against the original product, and retries flawed results before sending borderline cases to a human reviewer.
Its release comes with benchmark data that highlights a broader problem in AI-generated commerce imagery. In tests of 4,250 AI-generated images covering 850 real products across clothing, footwear, bags, jewellery, and accessories, the best image-editing models passed a full product fidelity check only 29% of the time.
Logos were distorted or unreadable in one in five outputs in those tests. Photoroom said its Fidelity Layer, used throughout the Visual Agents process, raised the pass rate to 38.2%.
Photoroom presents the issue as less about access to AI models and more about connecting tools, vendors, and review processes that can handle large catalogues without introducing inconsistent results. It says many businesses still rely on manual quality control because one model may succeed on one image and fail on another, even for the same product.
Company engineers found that repeated attempts could improve results without changing the underlying model. That led to the retry loop inside Visual Agents, which is meant to catch recoverable failures before human reviewers get involved.
Photoroom said several large marketplaces have already built internal systems to score and filter AI-generated product images. It argues that no equivalent commercial option has existed for companies without the resources to build those systems themselves.
Early deployments cited by Photoroom span marketplaces and retail platforms with large volumes of product photography. One unnamed consumer marketplace ran more than 1.5 million automated quality checks in three weeks and corrected more than 90,000 images after defects were found.
A food delivery marketplace processed 8,200 catalogue images in one overnight run, with 99.9% completed automatically and seven sent to a human reviewer, according to the company. A fashion resale marketplace recorded a 2.2% lift in gross merchandise value over seven days against a control group, with results ranging from 2% to 5% by product category, using Photoroom's Create & Transform API, which now runs inside Visual Agents.
Photoroom is focusing on reducing the labour involved in visual review at scale, particularly for retailers and marketplaces that process large numbers of product listings each day.
"I have run imaging operations that processed millions of products a year. The part nobody sees is the review queue. Every image that needs a person is a minute of somebody's day, and at catalog scale those minutes are headcount. Visual Agents cut that queue down to the images that genuinely need someone," said Jeff Strauss, Head of Imaging at Photoroom.
Matt Rouif described the company's view of the problem facing enterprise teams using AI for catalogue work.
"Almost every enterprise team we talk to describes the same problem. They have good models available to them, and they still cannot get a catalog they trust out the other end. That is not a model problem. It is everything around the model: knowing which one to use for which product, checking whether the result is good enough to sell, and fixing it when it is not. That work has been landing on our customers. We built Visual Agents so it lands on us instead," said Rouif.
Visual Agents is available to enterprise customers, with pricing based on volume. Photoroom also offers an added guarantee for customers with stricter fidelity requirements, covering cases that still fail after the system's retry process.
Founded in 2019, Photoroom says it processes more than seven billion images a year across mobile, web, and API services. Its customers include marketplaces and commerce platforms such as DoorDash and Depop, and it operates from Paris and New York.
The benchmark figures underline the challenge for retailers trying to automate catalogue production without changing how products appear to buyers: in Photoroom's tests, even the strongest AI image-editing models passed a full product fidelity check in fewer than three out of 10 cases.

title: Photoroom запускає Visual Agents для каталогів: моделі проходять перевірку лише у 29% випадків
lead: Photoroom представив Visual Agents — корпоративну систему, яка автоматизує AI-генерацію товарних фото й відео з перевіркою точності та повторними спробами, і оприлюднив бенчмарк точності моделей редагування.
full: Visual Agents будує пайплайн навколо вхідних каталожних зображень: обирає модель редагування під задачу, порівнює результат з оригіналом товару, повторює невдалі генерації і лише сумнівні випадки віддає людині. Продукт доступний для enterprise-клієнтів з оплатою за обсяг; для суворіших вимог є додаткова гарантія на кейси, які не проходять і після повторів.

Найцікавіше — бенчмарк: на 4 250 згенерованих зображеннях для 850 реальних товарів (одяг, взуття, сумки, прикраси) найкращі моделі редагування проходили повну перевірку точності лише у 29% випадків, а логотипи спотворювалися в кожному пʼятому результаті. Власний Fidelity Layer Photoroom підняв показник до 38,2%. Інженери помітили, що повторні спроби без зміни моделі помітно покращують результат — звідси retry-цикл.

Серед ранніх впроваджень: маркетплейс виконав понад 1,5 млн автоматичних перевірок за три тижні і виправив понад 90 тис. зображень; сервіс доставки їжі обробив 8 200 фото за ніч, з них 7 пішли рецензенту. Photoroom заявляє понад 7 млрд оброблених зображень на рік.
means: Photoroom (tier-2) рухається в enterprise-автоматизацію, де ми не конкуруємо, але його дані важливі: навіть найкращі моделі інпейнту спотворюють дрібні деталі й текст у більшості випадків. Для GenErase, GenSwap і GenExpand це аргумент за автоматичну перевірку результату й повторну генерацію під капотом, а не лише кнопку «ще варіант». Підхід «модель-роутер + перевірка + retry» можна перенести на наш хмарний пайплайн.

Diffusion, bloom and halation arrive in the Effects panel, applied globally or through masks – but not in Lightroom.
Adobe recently released the newest version of its Raw processing software, Adobe Camera Raw 18.6 . Its headline feature is a native Glow effect tool that gives users three analog-inspired looks – diffusion, bloom and halation – directly within ACR. Other features include a new Metadata Info Panel that shows image data directly in the editing workspace, and photographers and designers who work with composites gain a new Trim tool that makes everything outside a crop transparent, rather than leaving it as hidden pixels. The update also adds support for additional camera and lens profiles.
The new Glow tool lives in Camera Raw's Effects panel alongside the existing Vignette and Grain sliders. Adobe's documentation describes three selectable styles. Diffusion applies a hazy, film-like softening effect that spreads across the frame, similar to what a Black Mist or Pro Mist filter attached to your lens would achieve. Bloom produces a softer, more even glow confined to the highlights, which could be useful for misty scenes and waterfalls. Halation adds a colored halo effect around bright edges and light sources, similar to the warm, or red-orange fringing that appears on film when light reflects off the film base back through the emulsion.
Glow works inside Camera Raw's masking system, so the effect can be dialed up or down on a subject, a luminance range or a selected area, though the Style, Range, Spread and Warmth sub-settings are shared globally – masks control how much something glows, not the kind of glow.
Greg Benz, a digital photo educator (and a member of the DPReview community ), posted a helpful video on his YouTube channel illustrating the capabilities of ACR's new Glow tool, including examples of using masks to achieve localized results. If you're interested in learning more about it, we highly recommend giving it a watch.
One thing worth calling out: Glow is currently an ACR-only feature and isn't available in Lightroom. Though given the close relationship between the two applications, we wouldn't be surprised to see it show up in Lightroom at some point.
ACR's new Metadata Info Panel provides an easy way to see read-only metadata for any photo you're viewing in Camera Raw. Clicking the small "i" on the right-hand pane of ACR will display the camera model, lens, image dimensions, file size, capture date, copyright information, file name and caption (if present). It will also display any content credentials information embedded in the photo.
The new Metadata Info Panel displays the camera model, lens, image dimensions, file size, capture date, copyright information, file name and caption.
The new Trim tool is located in the Crop & Expand panel. It can be used to trim an image to the exact area you've selected, making everything outside the crop transparent rather than retaining it as hidden pixels. This is different than a normal crop in ACR, which is non-destructive, keeping the pixels outside the cropped area but not displaying them. This removes a step for photographers or designers creating composites or those who need transparent backgrounds.
Trim can also be used in conjunction with Generative Expand: trim to the area you want, then expand the canvas using generative content from Adobe Firefly.
According to Adobe, ACR 18.6 also supports additional cameras and lenses, including the Tamron 12-20mm F2.8 and Reeflex anamorphic and fisheye lenses for iPhone. As of this writing, Adobe hasn't updated its list of supported camera models since earlier in August; you can check the company's camera support page for the latest information.
ACR 18.6 is available now through the Creative Cloud desktop app. You can find the full release notes on Adobe's website with additional details in a post to the Adobe Community site.

title: Adobe Camera Raw 18.6: інструмент Glow з дифузією, bloom і галацією для RAW
lead: Adobe випустила Camera Raw 18.6 з новим інструментом Glow у панелі Effects: три плівкові стилі свічення — Diffusion, Bloom і Halation — застосовуються до RAW глобально або через маски. Також додано панель метаданих і інструмент Trim.
full: Glow розташований у панелі Effects поруч із Vignette і Grain. Diffusion дає туманне пом'якшення на кшталт фільтрів Black Mist / Pro Mist, Bloom — м'яке свічення лише у світлах (тумани, водоспади), Halation — кольоровий ореол навколо яскравих країв і джерел світла, як на плівці. Є підналаштування Style, Range, Spread і Warmth; вони спільні для всього кадру, а маски (об'єкт, діапазон яскравості, область) керують лише силою ефекту.

Нова панель Metadata Info показує камеру, об'єктив, розміри, дату, копірайт і Content Credentials прямо в робочому просторі. Інструмент Trim у Crop & Expand робить усе поза кадруванням прозорим (а не прихованим), що спрощує композитинг і працює в парі з Generative Expand на Firefly. Додано профілі нових камер і об'єктивів, зокрема Tamron 12-20mm F2.8 і анаморфних об'єктивів Reeflex для iPhone.
Оновлення доступне через Creative Cloud. Glow поки що є лише в ACR і відсутній у Lightroom, але оглядачі очікують його появу там пізніше — так само, як раніше з видаленням відблисків.
means: Adobe додає плівкові ефекти на рівні RAW, які в Luminar Neo частково покриваються Film Grain, Vignette і Magic Light AI, але окремого дифузійного свічення з керуванням Bloom/Halation і теплотою в нас немає. Це недорогий у реалізації класичний ефект, який добре лягає в Presets і Layers та може працювати з Mask AI для локального застосування. Варто оцінити його і для Luminar Mobile як on-device фільтр.

Remember Where You Put Important Items in “Find Hub”
A new feature is rolling out that lets you have “Gemini” remember where you placed important items and save that location information in the “Find Hub” app.
For items that cannot take a Bluetooth tracker, such as a passport or spare keys, you can simply say something like, “Ok Google, remember that I put my passport in the bedroom drawer,” and the location of the item will be automatically recorded, optionally with an attached photo. When you want to find it, just ask “Gemini” for the location or check the “Remembered Items” tab within the “Find Hub” app.
The “Remembered Items” tab in the “Find Hub” app does not track the real-time location of items, and accuracy depends on the information entered by the user. “Find Hub” is available on devices running Android 16 or later in countries and regions where “Gemini” and “Find Hub” are supported.
Motion Sickness Reduction with “Motion Assist”
“Motion Assist” is a new feature that helps reduce motion sickness while continuing to use your smartphone during travel.
It is designed to bridge the gap between what your eyes see and the movement of the vehicle by displaying subtle, animated bubble overlays on the screen that move in sync with the vehicle’s motion. You can set it to turn on automatically when traveling, add it to your Quick Settings tiles, and customize the shape, color, and opacity of the bubbles to your preference.
“Motion Assist” is available globally and in all languages on smartphones powered by “Android 17.”
A new feature called “Guided vision” is rolling out to “Gemini Live,” allowing you to share your camera and receive audio descriptions about what is right in front of you.
Designed for and with the blind and low-vision community, the new “Guided vision” feature in “Gemini Live” helps you read small text on food labels, order from a menu in a dimly lit restaurant, or identify items around the house. If the camera is misaligned, audio feedback guides you to adjust the camera angle, pan across space, or center the subject to ensure you get the answers you need.
For quick access to “Guided vision,” you can add it to your Accessibility shortcut or enable it directly from the TalkBack menu or Gemini app settings. It will be rolling out soon in countries where Gemini is available on devices running Android 9 or later.
“Google Keep” Integration in Google Messages
“Google Keep” is being integrated into the “Google Messages” app, allowing you to share and update shopping lists, travel notes, and more without ever leaving your chat.
With “Google Keep” integrated into the “Google Messages” app, everyone in a group can view, edit, and add to lists and notes, enabling seamless real-time collaboration without switching apps. Simply tap the “+” icon in the chat screen within the “Google Messages” app to bring up “Google Keep.”
Rolling out globally across all languages starting today. Note that enabling RCS is required.
The “Chat Themes” feature in the “Google Messages” app now lets you customize unique backgrounds and color schemes for individual chats.
With the “Chat Themes” feature, selecting a wallpaper or using your own photo automatically adjusts text bubble colors to match harmoniously, and you can also freely change colors to craft your preferred style. Note that “Chat Themes” are only visible to the person who created the theme. Enabling RCS is also required.
The “Chat Themes” feature in the “Google Messages” app is available globally and in all languages.
Google Messages Adopts “Remix (Nano Banana 2)”
The image generation feature “Remix” in the “Google Messages” app now adopts the “Nano Banana 2” generative AI model, enabling image generation with sharper text rendering and broader world knowledge.
You can create party invitations or feature your friends in a movie poster without ever leaving the “Google Messages” app.
The “Google Photos” app is adding an “AI Enhance” feature that eliminates tedious editing tasks and makes your favorite photos shine with a single tap.
“AI Enhance” in the “Google Photos” app analyzes your photos and instantly applies the most effective corrections, such as color toning and cropping. It is available globally across all languages.
The “Google Photos” app is adding “Ask Photos,” an AI image editing feature that applies edits in seconds simply by describing what you want, eliminating the need to choose tools or adjust sliders.
Edits like removing people from the background or adding new elements to a scene can be completed just by talking to it. The “Ask Photos” AI image editing feature is available in the US, UK, Germany, India, France, Italy, Australia, Spain, and Japan, in English, French, German, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Italian, Marathi, Spanish, Tamil, Telugu, and Japanese.
“Search Live,” the conversational AI search feature in the “Google” app that has already been rolling out in Japan, is expanding its availability globally for all languages.
The conversational feature “Gemini Live” is now powered by the “Nano Banana” generative AI model, allowing you to transform images of your surrounding scenery simply by pointing your camera and talking.
Out loud, you can request to redecorate your bedroom or feature a friend in a Renaissance painting, and your idea will be generated as a new image in seconds. “Nano Banana” image transformation in “Gemini Live” is available on Android 10 and later.
The conversational feature “Gemini Live” is now available in the car operating system “Android Auto.”

Following the announcement at I/O 2026 in May, Google Pics is launching in general availability today.
Google Pics, which comes after Google Vids , is “built natively into Google Workspace.” You can click on an image in Google Docs or Slides and access the Pics editor as an overlay to start editing. An update in the coming weeks will let you edit images uploaded to Google Drive.
You can also access the tool from pics.new:
Besides generating a new image (with multiple options offered), you can import files from your computer, Google Drive, or Google Photos to start editing.
Leveraging Nano Banana, Google Pics offers “precise, object-based image editing.” Tools let you:
Select and edit individual objects within an image
Edit, reformat, or even translate individual text elements
Crop your image for web, social media, print, or digital
Process multiple edits at once, and revert any unwanted changes easily
The object segmentation capability lets you isolate a specific part and leave other parts of the image untouched. After selecting, you just provide text comments with the ability to “execute multiple edits at once.” Similarly, you can edit text that appears in images without changing anything else, which also allows for translation.
Pics eliminates the frustration of wrangling pixels and feeling like you need to be a graphic designer to deliver a great image.

Для Luminar Mobile важливо, що імпорт іде прямо з Google Photos і що рівень «виділив об'єкт — описав правку» стає базовим очікуванням користувача. We have finally reached the developer beta of iOS 27, and with it comes the AI-powered Clean Up tool for editing photos and removing unwanted elements. This tool, whose maturity we have long awaited, finally feels like it is worth actually using to edit our daily photos and make them look perfect with a single touch on our iPhone. But as is often the case with Apple, there is a major hurdle we must address that makes a real difference in the daily user experience.
When testing the Clean Up tool in the iOS 27 developer beta, the smart touches Apple has added are clearly visible. The tool has become much faster and more accurate at identifying elements the user wants to remove from the photo background. Apple’s AI seems to have learned how to handle complex details like lighting and shadows better than ever before.
The beauty of these first impressions is that the tool no longer feels like a poorly performing experimental feature; it has become a real tool that photographers and iPhone owners can rely on to get rid of annoying details in their favorite shots without distorting the original image, finally making it a tool worth using.
If we compare current performance to how it was in iOS 26, we notice a huge leap in quality. In the previous system, the Clean Up tool would sometimes leave blurry spots or inconsistent colors where the element was removed, making the edit look inaccurate or obvious to a trained eye. In iOS 27, Apple has largely addressed this issue by improving the generative AI-based fill algorithms.
The results now look very natural, as the new system can understand the general pattern of the background and reconstruct it with intelligence that rivals professional photo editing applications. This represents a major success for Apple’s software engineers and a real evolution we have been eagerly awaiting.
The dilemma of choice: Fast vs. High Quality
One of the most important new additions to the Clean Up tool in iOS 27 is the option for the user to choose between two editing modes: Fast and High Quality. This option gives you great flexibility; if you want a quick edit to share on social media immediately, the Fast mode will get the job done in a fraction of a second.
However, if you are looking for a perfect, flawless shot for memories or printing, the High Quality mode takes a little extra time but provides ultra-precise processing for every pixel in the image. But always remember, despite all these flashy features, there is a major hurdle regarding performance and system compatibility that might make some users hesitate before relying on it fully during this beta phase.

DxO is making PhotoLab 10 available today, with some solid new features and improvements to the existing ones. PhotoLab has become increasingly popular among raw editors because of its power and the inclusion of the DxO technology that adjusts for specific lens and camera combinations. These corrections are applied automatically upon opening a file if you use the default DxO Style – Natural preset, providing a sharp, geometrically accurate starting point before manual editing.
I've heard from more than a few professional photographers who have switched from the more popular editors, mainly Adobe, for a variety of reasons, including subscriptions and issues with support.
Here's some of what's new in PhotoLab 10, and I'll have my thoughts as well:
DxO PhotoLab 10 introduces Depth Masks, a new way to create local adjustments based on distance from the camera rather than shape or color. Using AI to analyze the image and generate a detailed depth map, Depth Masks allow photographers to precisely target foreground, midground, or background elements without requiring embedded depth data.
After applying a filter or adjustment, photographers can use intuitive sliders and adjustable feathering handles to refine exactly where the effect appears within the scene. The result is smooth, natural transitions and highly precise selective edits that would otherwise require complex and time-consuming manual masking.
A streamlined interface centered around a single color wheel allows photographers to independently adjust shadows, midtones, highlights, and overall color balance, making it easy to shape the mood and atmosphere of an image.
For even greater creative control, color adjustments can be linked across tonal ranges, preserving their relative relationship while exploring different looks. The result is a faster, more intuitive approach to color grading that offers both flexibility and consistency.
AI Masks can now identify every person within a scene, allowing photographers to create a single mask for all people, combine selected people into one mask, or generate individual masks for as many people—or individual features of people such as eyes, hair, and lips—as needed. This makes group portraits and complex scenes faster and easier to refine.
Face segmentation brings new precision to portrait editing, adding eyebrows, eyes, iris and pupil, sclera, teeth, facial hair, facial skin, and lips to the list of selectable AI Mask categories. Alongside existing options such as sky, subject, background, people, animals, flowers, and vehicles, these new categories help photographers target detailed adjustments more efficiently.
AI Masks can now be refined using DxO’s renowned U Point technology, which intelligently selects areas based on color and luminosity. After creating an AI-powered selection, photographers can use the familiar U Point eyedropper to expand or contract the selection, making it easy to fine-tune complex selections without resorting to manual painting.
DxO PhotoLab 10 also introduces AI-powered dust removal at the raw level, automatically detecting and removing sensor dust and small imperfections before they interrupt the editing process.
DxO PhotoLab 10 expands these capabilities with a new Control Brush and the ability to switch Control Points from circular to elliptical, giving photographers greater flexibility when creating local adjustments. The Control Brush combines the familiarity of traditional brush painting with U Point’s intelligent color- and luminosity-based selection, while elliptical Control Points provide a more natural fit for many subjects. Combined with AI Masks and the new Depth Masks, these tools allow photographers to choose the most effective selection method for every image, then refine masks using whichever technology best suits the task. Sophisticated local adjustments become faster, more intuitive, and more precise.
Reviewers got an advance copy of the software, and I've had one update as release day approached. I've been impressed with PhotoLab for a few years since I first started using the software. It takes some getting used to if you've spent your life in Lightroom or Photoshop, but after a while you get the hang of it.
I was very impressed with the Depth Masks feature. It is easy to select where you want to adjust lighting because of the DxO advanced AI selections. I also have liked the Luminar Neo lighting depth adjustments, and it has a very easy on-screen way to adjust the light, but PhotoLab is very easy to use and gives you more power to make adjustments.
Here I've used PhotoLab AI to select the areas I want to adjust:
Then, using the sliders, it was easy to change the lighting:
PhotoLab has all the usual sliders seen in other raw editors, so there's not much to say there. Color grading is easy with the color wheel GUI, but color grading does take practice, and it's not hard to get into trouble.
PhotoLab advertises AI, and that is used mainly for smart selections and masking. You won't find generative AI here or the ability Adobe has to create something from nothing in your images. That will be a negative to some editors, a positive to others. So, no sky replacement, generative erase, etc. DxO focuses on technical image purity and traditional editing.
One thing I didn't like was advertising within the interface. Several times I was offered a chance to buy DxO products like its film-emulation product FilmPack. That stuff just doesn't belong in a pro-level editor, and I hope they stop doing it.
DxO isn't a click-on-it-and-you-are-ready-to-go editor. There's a lot on screen, and the controls aren't always consistent. Sometimes I have to click on a control to turn it off. Sometimes the Escape key exits the function.
Still, PhotoLab 10 is an extremely powerful editor, and with power comes some complicated operations. I'd love to see the overall user interface simplified a bit more, but there's no denying this is one very powerful and elegant editor.
Even my beta was reliable with no surprises
The feature set is incredible, and you'll take some time learning all it can do
It is unsurpassed in doing complicated masking selections, and it makes the selections painless
Color controls and noise reduction are best in class, as are the tools for lens and camera matching
The depth masking is a game changer, surpassing anything on offer elsewhere and giving you control of lighting
Would like to see more beginner tutorials from DxO to ease the transition to this software
A rethink of the user interface would be positive. Some icons are very small, and controls can be hard to find
Having ads in the user interface was a bad decision. There are better ways to learn about the other fine DxO products
Make no mistake, this very powerful raw editor has made a significant leap forward in version 10. Yes, I have a few niggles here and there, but as a landscape photographer, I can really turn out photos I am proud of. Kudos to the DxO team for offering a powerful alternative to other raw editors on the market.

title: DxO PhotoLab 10: маски глибини, сегментація обличчя, кольорове колесо та зв'язка з Affinity
lead: DxO випустила PhotoLab 10 з новими Depth Masks на основі AI-карти глибини, сегментацією облич, масками для кожної людини окремо, єдиним колесом колорграду та кнопкою передачі зображення в Affinity. Довічна ліцензія коштує $249.99, апгрейд з версій 8–9 — $129.99.
full: Depth Masks будують карту глибини з будь-якого файлу без вбудованих даних глибини й дозволяють локально редагувати передній, середній або задній план; межі уточнюються повзунками й розтушовкою. AI Masks тепер розпізнають кожну людину окремо (спільна маска, група або індивідуальні маски), а сегментація обличчя додає брови, очі, райдужку і зіницю, склеру, зуби, волосся на обличчі, шкіру та губи до наявних категорій (небо, суб'єкт, фон, тварини, квіти, транспорт). AI-маски можна уточнювати піпеткою U Point за кольором і яскравістю.

Новий інструмент Color Grading зібраний навколо одного колеса з незалежним керуванням тінями, середніми тонами, світлами й балансом; правки можна зв'язувати між тональними діапазонами. Додано Control Brush, еліптичні контрольні точки, автоматичне видалення сенсорного пилу на рівні RAW, кадрування «як знято», покращення бібліотеки. Оновлення шумозаглушення немає — використовується той самий DeepPRIME, що й у PureRAW 6. Генеративних функцій, заміни неба чи генеративного видалення в PhotoLab, як і раніше, немає.

Кнопка Affinity відкриває зображення для попіксельної ретуші й композитингу з поверненням результату в PhotoLab — DxO називає це першим кроком інтеграції. Оглядачі підкреслюють, що зв'язка DxO + Affinity утворює повний RAW-to-pixel робочий процес без підписки, а Fstoppers окремо порівнює Depth Masks із «регулюванням світла за глибиною» в Luminar Neo, відзначаючи більшу гнучкість DxO. Доступна 7-денна пробна версія.
means: DxO виходить на нашу територію: Depth Masks за AI-картою глибини прямо конкурують із Relight AI і Bokeh AI, а посегментна маска обличчя (райдужка, склера, зуби, губи) деталізованіша за наші Face AI/Skin AI та Mask AI. Водночас у PhotoLab немає Sky AI, GenErase та інших генеративних інструментів — це наша перевага в позиціюванні. Зв'язка «довічна ліцензія + Affinity» цілить у ту ж аудиторію, що тримає Luminar другим редактором поруч із Lightroom.

OpenShot 4.0 is out now for Windows , macOS , and Linux , the first major version since 3.5.1 in April. It is still free under GPLv3.
Color View arranges a preview, clip properties, color wheels, and video scopes around the footage. It is driven by a new Color Grade effect covering exposure, contrast, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, saturation, and vibrance, with separate wheels for global, shadow, midtone, and highlight ranges. You also get four editable curves for the full image and the red, green, and blue channels.
OpenShot reads .cube LUT files and includes an intensity control that blends a LUT instead of applying it at full strength. Every parameter is keyframable. Scopes cover luma waveform, histogram, RGB parade, and vectorscope, each with a region tool for analyzing part of a frame; the vectorscope adds a skin-tone reference line.
Recording View, on the other hand, captures microphone, screen, webcam, and system audio direclty into a project. It keeps each source as a separate file and timeline clip. Screen and webcam takes can be placed into a rounded picture-in-picture layout automatically. Capture paths are native to Windows, macOS, Linux X11, and Linux Wayland through PipeWire; however, there are options varying by system and permissions.
Ten effects are new: Audio Visualization, Beat Sync, Film Grain, Denoise Image, Shadow, Glow, Displacement Map, Timer, Color Grade, and Object Mask. The last of those builds an animated selection around a subject from a few positive and negative points, using YOLO, EfficientSAM, and Cutie networks converted to ONNX and downloaded on demand. All processing happens locally, with no cloud service, account, or subscription involved.
Also, the timeline is now fully native Qt. It replaces the old web-based components, and ruler timecode can be edited directly.

title: OpenShot 4.0: офлайн AI-маскування об'єктів на YOLO, EfficientSAM і Cutie
lead: Вийшов безкоштовний відеоредактор OpenShot 4.0 (GPLv3) для Windows, macOS і Linux. Серед нових ефектів — Object Mask, що будує анімовану маску навколо об'єкта за кількома точками повністю локально, без хмари й акаунта.
full: Object Mask використовує мережі YOLO, EfficientSAM і Cutie, конвертовані в ONNX і завантажувані за потреби; користувач ставить кілька позитивних і негативних точок, а маска трекається по кадрах. Уся обробка відбувається на пристрої. Серед десяти нових ефектів також Denoise Image, Film Grain, Glow, Shadow, Displacement Map і Color Grade.

Новий Color View об'єднує колірні кола для глобального, тіньового, середнього та світлого діапазонів, чотири криві, підтримку .cube LUT з регулюванням інтенсивності та скопи: waveform, гістограму, RGB parade і vectorscope з лінією шкірних тонів. Таймлайн переписано на нативний Qt, а Recording View дозволяє записувати екран, вебкамеру й мікрофон одразу в проєкт.
means: Це референс для Mask AI і Erase: зв'язка EfficientSAM + Cutie в ONNX показує, що інтерактивне маскування за кліками з трекінгом можна робити повністю на пристрої в open-source продукті. Для Luminar Mobile, де Erase і Portrait частково залежать від хмари, EfficientSAM під Core ML/NNAPI — реальний кандидат на локальний вибір об'єкта. GPLv3 не дозволяє брати код напряму, але самі моделі мають окремі ліцензії й їх варто перевірити.

RIYADH — August 31, 2026 — Today at LEAP 2026, Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) — the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms — announced an expanded partnership with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) and HUMAIN, a PIF company, delivering full-stack artificial intelligence capabilities globally, to advance Saudi Arabia’s thriving creative sector. Adobe’s commitment is valued at over $4 billion.
Adobe’s mission is to empower everyone to create. The partnership also advances Adobe’s strategy of expanding access to its AI solutions that power creativity, productivity and customer experience.
Adobe Firefly , the all-in-one AI creative studio, brings together industry-leading AI models, Adobe’s pro-grade editing tools and agentic capabilities. From brainstorming and visualizing ideas to generating and editing images, video, audio and design assets, Firefly brings every stage of creative work together from ideation to creation to production.

Photography technology has changed dramatically over the past two decades, but one principle remains central for Capture One : understanding how photographers actually work.
For CEO Rafael Orta, developing new tools is not simply about predicting trends. It starts with conversations, studio visits and listening to the people using the software every day.
"One of the things that I am personally most proud of about Capture One is that we speak to thousands of photographers every year," says Orta.
"And this is not an exaggeration or a number that I just picked out of thin air."
Capture One regularly attends major photography events around the world, including industry shows, conferences, school visits and studio sessions.
But Orta says the relationship goes beyond simply showing products.
"We are a company that is truly, truly connected with the industry," he explains.
